title: Hereditary discrepancy and factorization norms (AimPL) — Problem 1.65: Tusnády's problem

problems.sourceStatement: Let $d_n$ be the discrepancy of $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$ wrt all alix-aligned rectangles i.e. the set system comprises of all axis-aligned rectangles in $\mathbb{R}^2$ as sets, maximised over all choices of $n$ points. Tusnady's problem then asks for the exact value of $d_n$. We can also ask for the same question in $\mathbb{R}^d$.
problems.problem: Tusnády's problem: determine the combinatorial discrepancy $d_d(n)$ of $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with respect to axis-parallel boxes. In the plane the known bounds are $\Omega(\log n) \leq d_2(n) \leq O(\log^2 n)$; in $\mathbb{R}^d$ they are $\Omega(\log^{d-1} n) \leq d_d(n) \leq O(\log^{d-1/2} n)$. Close the gap (the conjectured truth is $\Theta(\log^{d-1} n)$).
problems.wordDescription: Tusnády's problem asks for the worst-case discrepancy of axis-parallel boxes with respect to $n$-point sets: color the points red/blue so that every box is as balanced as possible. It is the combinatorial analogue of the classical (Lebesgue-measure) discrepancy of boxes, which is $\Theta(\log n)$ in the plane (Schmidt) and open in higher dimensions. Beck (1981) established the connection and proved $O(\log^4 n)$ in the plane; subsequent work brought the planar upper bound down to $O(\log^{2.5} n)$ (the state of the art at the time of the workshop), then to $O(\log^2 n)$ (Bansal-Garg 2017), and the $d$-dimensional bound to $O_d(\log^d n)$ (Bansal-Garg) and $O(\log^{d-1/2} n)$ (Nikolov 2017). The lower bound $\Omega(\log^{d-1} n)$ follows from the $\gamma_2$-norm characterization of hereditary discrepancy (Matoušek-Nikolov-Talwar). The remaining gap is a single $\sqrt{\log n}$ factor in every dimension; it is conjectured that $d_d(n) = \Theta(\log^{d-1} n)$, and even the planar case $d_2(n) = \Theta(\log n)$ is open.
problems.mathematicalConditions: Setting. For a finite set $P \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ let $\mathcal{B}_d(P) = \{P \cap B : B = \prod_{i=1}^d [a_i, b_i]\}$ be the set system induced by axis-parallel boxes, $\mathrm{disc}(P) = \min_{\chi : P \to \{-1,1\}} \max_{S \in \mathcal{B}_d(P)} |\sum_{x \in S} \chi(x)|$, and $d_d(n) = \max_{|P| = n} \mathrm{disc}(P)$ (it suffices to consider anchored boxes $\prod [0, b_i]$, up to a factor $2^d$). Problem. Determine the order of growth of $d_d(n)$ for each fixed $d \geq 2$. Conjecture: $d_d(n) = \Theta(\log^{d-1} n)$. Benchmarks. Lower bounds: $d_2(n) = \Omega(\log n)$ (from Schmidt's geometric lower bound / directly), and $d_d(n) = \Omega(\log^{d-1} n)$ for all $d$ (Matoušek-Nikolov-Talwar, via $\gamma_2$). Upper bounds: $d_2(n) = O(\log^4 n)$ (Beck 1981), improved in steps to $O(\log^{2.5} n)$ (the best bound before 2016) and then to $d_2(n) = O(\log^2 n)$ (Bansal-Garg 2017); in general $d_d(n) = O_d(\log^{d+1/2} n)$ (pre-2016), $O_d(\log^d n)$ (Bansal-Garg 2017), and $d_d(n) = O(\log^{d-1/2} n)$ (Nikolov 2017, using Banaszczyk's theorem on signed series). Hence $\Omega(\log^{d-1} n) \leq d_d(n) \leq O(\log^{d-1/2} n)$ for all $d \geq 2$; the gap is $\sqrt{\log n}$. All upper bounds are attained by polynomial-time algorithms. Complete resolution. Determining $d_d(n)$ up to constant factors for every fixed $d$ (e.g. proving $d_d(n) = O(\log^{d-1} n)$, or a lower bound $d_d(n) = \Omega(\log^{d-1/2} n)$). Minimal progress that counts as a solution of this record. Any of: (i) $d_2(n) = O(\log^{2-\delta} n)$ for some constant $\delta > 0$, or $d_2(n) = \Omega(\log^{1+\delta} n)$; (ii) for some fixed $d \geq 3$, $d_d(n) = O(\log^{d - 1/2 - \delta} n)$ or $d_d(n) = \Omega(\log^{d-1+\delta} n)$; (iii) the conjecture $d_d(n) = O(\log^{d-1} n)$ for all product point sets $P = P_1 \times \dots \times P_d$ (in particular all grids), for some $d \geq 2$ where it is not already known; (iv) determining the hereditary discrepancy of boxes up to constants (currently between $\Omega(\log^{d-1} n)$ and $O(\log^{d-1/2} n)$, the same range as $d_d(n)$). Improving constants or $\log\log n$ factors does not count.

literature.title: W. M. Schmidt, Irregularities of distribution VII, Acta Arithmetica 21:45-50, 1972
literature.description: The $\Omega(\log n)$ lower bound for the (geometric) discrepancy of axis-parallel rectangles in the unit square, which underlies the planar lower bound $d_2(n) = \Omega(\log n)$.

literature.title: J. Beck, Balanced two-colorings of finite sets in the square I, Combinatorica 1(4):327-335, 1981
literature.description: Introduces Tusnády's problem (posed by G. Tusnády) and proves the first upper bound $O(\log^4 n)$ in the plane, establishing the transference between geometric and combinatorial discrepancy of boxes.

literature.title: J. Matoušek, A. Nikolov, K. Talwar, Factorization norms and hereditary discrepancy, International Mathematics Research Notices 2020(3):751-780 (arXiv 2014)
literature.description: Shows that hereditary discrepancy is characterized up to logarithmic factors by the factorization norm $\gamma_2$ ($\gamma_2(A)/O(\log m) \leq \mathrm{herdisc}(A) \leq O(\sqrt{\log m})\,\gamma_2(A)$); as an application derives the lower bound $\Omega(\log^{d-1} n)$ for Tusnády's problem in $\mathbb{R}^d$.

literature.title: N. Bansal, S. Garg, Algorithmic discrepancy beyond partial coloring, STOC 2017; arXiv:1611.01805
literature.description: General algorithmic framework that overcomes the iterated-partial-coloring loss. For Tusnády's problem it improves the planar bound from $O(\log^{2.5} n)$ to $O(\log^2 n)$ and gives $O_d(\log^d n)$ for boxes in $\mathbb{R}^d$ (since improved to $O(\log^{d-1/2} n)$ by Nikolov). For the Steinitz problem it gives the first algorithm matching Banaszczyk's non-constructive $\ell_\infty$ bound and an algorithmic $O(\sqrt{d \log n})$ bound in the $\ell_2$ case.

literature.title: A. Nikolov, Tighter bounds for the discrepancy of boxes and polytopes, SoCG 2017; Mathematika 63(3):1091-1113, 2017
literature.description: Proves the upper bound $O(\log^{d-1/2} n)$ for Tusnády's problem in $\mathbb{R}^d$ (improving the $O_d(\log^d n)$ of Bansal-Garg) by combining the factorization-norm approach with Banaszczyk's theorem on signed series; extends the bound to dilates and translates of a fixed convex polytope, with nearly matching lower bounds.

literature.title: N. Bansal, A. Nikolov, Discrepancy theory: an algorithmic and geometric perspective, arXiv:2608.00140, 2026
literature.description: 2026 survey of combinatorial discrepancy (Komlós, Beck-Fiala, Tusnády, vector balancing and the algorithmic theory); cited here as the reference for the current state of these problems, in particular for Tusnády's problem ($\Omega(\log n) \leq d_2(n) \leq O(\log^2 n)$ in the plane, $\Omega(\log^{d-1} n) \leq d_d(n) \leq O(\log^{d-1/2} n)$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$) and for the state of the Komlós and Beck-Fiala conjectures before their resolution in arXiv:2609.11189 (September 2026).

problems.verificationNotes: Re-verified on 2026-09-20 against http://aimpl.org/hereddiscrep/1/, the arXiv abstracts of Bansal-Garg (arXiv:1611.01805), Nikolov (arXiv:1701.05532) and Matoušek-Nikolov-Talwar (arXiv:1408.1376), and the 2026 survey arXiv:2608.00140. Corrections made on 2026-09-20 following the comment by Richard Peng: the planar lower bound is $\Omega(\log n)$ (the earlier record wrote $O(\log n)$); the planar upper bound is $O(\log^2 n)$ (Bansal-Garg), not $O(\log^{2.5} n)$; the higher-dimensional upper bound is $O(\log^{d-1/2} n)$ (Nikolov), not $\log^{d+1/2} n$; Nikolov's paper is now cited directly. The sourceStatement preserves the original AimPL wording (including its typography) as historical text; the corrected bounds are in problem/statusDetails/mathematicalConditions.
problems.statusDetails: In $\mathbb{R}^2$: $\Omega(\log n) \leq d_2(n) \leq O(\log^2 n)$ (lower bound classical/Schmidt-type; upper bound Bansal-Garg 2017, improving Larsen's $O(\log^{2.5} n)$). In $\mathbb{R}^d$: $\Omega(\log^{d-1} n) \leq d_d(n) \leq O(\log^{d-1/2} n)$ (lower bound Matoušek-Nikolov-Talwar; upper bound Nikolov 2017, improving Bansal-Garg's $O_d(\log^d n)$ and the earlier $O_d(\log^{d+1/2} n)$). All upper bounds are algorithmic.
